literal: Thereupon in the fifth month he executed Yuan Shizhe, Jingwu, and twenty-five other households; the remaining nineteen households were all placed under prohibition.
idiomatic: In the fifth month he executed Yuan Shizhe, Jingwu, and twenty-five other households; nineteen more households were placed under prohibition.

literal: Shao was confined in the capital's dungeon, starved, and died eating his sleeve.
idiomatic: Shao was shut in the capital dungeon, starved, and died gnawing his sleeve.

literal: By the seventh month there was a great slaughter of the Yuan clan; from Zhaocheng down none were left.
idiomatic: By the seventh month the Yuan were slaughtered wholesale; from Zhaocheng's line down, none were spared.

literal: Some had fathers or grandfathers who had been kings, some had themselves long been eminent, some had strong brothers—all were beheaded at the eastern market.
idiomatic: Some had fathers or grandfathers who had been kings, some had long held high rank, some had strong brothers in their prime—all were beheaded at the eastern market.

literal: Infants were tossed into the air and caught on spears.
idiomatic: Infants were tossed into the air and caught on spears.

literal: Before and after, seven hundred twenty-one died in all; all corpses were cast into the Zhang River.
idiomatic: Seven hundred twenty-one died in all; every corpse was cast into the Zhang River.

literal: Those who cut open fish often found fingernails; for a long time the capital would not eat fish.
idiomatic: Men who gutted fish often found fingernails; for a long season the capital would not touch fish.

literal: Shizhe's cousin Huangtou was made with other prisoners to ride paper kites from the Golden Phoenix Terrace and fly; Huangtou alone reached Zimo Lane before falling; he was handed to the censor's prison and Bi Yiyun starved him to death.
idiomatic: Shizhe's cousin Huangtou was set with other prisoners to ride paper kites from the Golden Phoenix Terrace; Huangtou alone reached Zimo Lane before he fell, was sent to the censor's prison, and Bi Yiyun starved him to death.

literal: Prince of Beihai Xiang, styled Jiyu, had a handsome countenance and graceful bearing.
idiomatic: Prince of Beihai Xiang, styled Jiyu, was handsome of face and graceful in bearing.

literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed and made attendant-in-ordinary.
idiomatic: In Taihe 9 he was enfeoffed and made attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: When Xiaowen toured north from Luoyang, Xiang was often with Attendant-in-Ordinary Prince of Pengcheng Xie in the carriage, attending left and right.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen toured north from Luoyang, Xiang often rode beside Prince of Pengcheng Xie in the imperial carriage, attending left and right.

literal: At the place where Emperor Wencheng shot the inscription, the emperor halted the carriage and ordered the younger princes and attending ministers all to try shooting near and far.
idiomatic: At the spot where Emperor Wencheng had shot his inscription, the emperor halted and ordered younger princes and attending ministers to try their skill at near and far targets.

literal: All others were twenty or thirty paces off; only Xiang's arrow reached it.
idiomatic: Others stood twenty or thirty paces back; only Xiang's arrow reached the mark.

literal: The emperor clapped his hands and laughed with delight; he then ordered the inscription cut and personally composed the text.
idiomatic: The emperor clapped and laughed with delight, then ordered the inscription carved and wrote the text himself.

literal: When the carriage campaigned south, Xiang served as acting commander of the palace guard and remained to defend.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign Xiang served as acting commander of the palace guard and remained behind to defend.

literal: When Xiaowen was near death he entrusted Xiang as Minister of Works to assist in government.
idiomatic: At his deathbed Xiaowen entrusted government to Xiang as minister of works.

literal: When Xuandi took government, he was made Grand General and Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xuandi took the reins, Xiang was made grand general and director of the secretariat.

literal: When Prince of Xianyang Xi plotted rebellion, Xiang memorialized asking to resign his duties; the order would not allow it.
idiomatic: When Prince of Xianyang Xi plotted rebellion, Xiang asked to resign; the throne would not allow it.

literal: He was made Grand Commandant, holding Minister of Works and Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat as before.
idiomatic: He was made grand commandant while retaining minister of works, attendant-in-ordinary, and director of the secretariat.

literal: The night Xiang received the appointment, a violent wind with thunder and lightning uprooted the paulownia in his court, a tree ten arm-spans around, which stood inverted in its place.
idiomatic: The night he received the appointment a storm wind with thunder uprooted the paulownia in his court, ten arm-spans around, and left it standing upside down in its hole.

literal: At first, when Xuandi took government, Xiang heard that Prince of Pengcheng Xie had the worry of overshadowing the ruler and wished to seize his post as Minister of Works; he greatly feared public opinion and therefore took Grand General; only now did he hold it.
idiomatic: When Xuandi first took power, Xiang had heard that Prince of Pengcheng Xie might overshadow the throne and had wanted his post as minister of works; fearing public talk, he took grand general instead—only now did he hold it.

literal: Heaven's authority was thus; those who knew saw he would not end well.
idiomatic: Heaven had spoken; those who understood knew he would not end well.

literal: Already favored as the emperor's younger uncle, his rank and repute at the summit, he was greedy without end and traded in public and private.
idiomatic: Favored as the emperor's younger uncle, rank and repute at their height, he was greedy without end and trafficked in public and private gain.

literal: He also staked out a residence outside the east side gate; there were even mourning coffins in the rooms; he asked to delay until the burial and was not granted it; the bier blocked the lane and passersby sighed in grief.
idiomatic: He staked out a mansion outside the east side gate; mourning coffins still stood in the rooms. He begged delay until the burial and was refused; biers blocked the lane and passersby sighed.

literal: Xiang's mother Grand Consort Gao greatly aided his violence; resentment in the neighborhood was loud.
idiomatic: His mother, Grand Consort Gao, fed his violence; the neighborhood seethed with complaint.

literal: His consort was daughter of Song Prince Liu Chang; she was not answered with ritual courtesy.
idiomatic: His consort was a daughter of Song Prince Liu Chang; he never treated her with the courtesy owed a wife.

literal: His favored concubine Lady Fan was loved as an equal partner.
idiomatic: His favored concubine Lady Fan he loved as an equal partner.

literal: After her death and burial he still destroyed the tomb passage to look in.
idiomatic: After her death and burial he still broke open the tomb passage to look upon her.

literal: He also had illicit relations with the consort of Prince of Anding Xie, Lady Gao—elder sister of Ru Hao's wife.
idiomatic: He also lay with the consort of Prince of Anding Xie, Lady Gao, elder sister to Ru Hao's wife.

literal: Xiang had long been attached to Hao; he also joined through licentious fondness, coming and going in close intimacy.
idiomatic: Xiang had long clung to Ru Hao and, through shared appetite for vice, came and went in close intimacy.

literal: Though Xiang was greedy and extravagant, Xuandi's ritual respect was still lofty.
idiomatic: Though Xiang was greedy and extravagant, the emperor's ritual respect still ran high.

literal: He often lived separately in the western corner of the Hualin Park, adjoining the capital pavilion palaces.
idiomatic: He often lived apart in the western corner of Hualin Park, adjoining the capital pavilion palaces.

literal: The emperor often stole to his place, drinking all day, meeting Grand Consort Gao; he called her Foster Mother, crawled to offer wine, with ritual like family.
idiomatic: The emperor often stole to his house and drank the day through, meeting Grand Consort Gao, calling her Foster Mother, crawling to offer wine with the ease of kin.

literal: On leaving, Gao always bowed in send-off, raising the cup and praying: "May Your Majesty live ten thousand years; once a year enter the house of me and my son."
idiomatic: On leaving, Gao always bowed him out, raising her cup: "May Your Majesty live ten thousand years and once a year enter the house of me and my son."

literal: At first, when Xuandi took government in person, Xiang with Prince of Xianyang Xi and Prince of Pengcheng Xie were all summoned in, riding together in a calf cart under strict guard.
idiomatic: When Xuandi first took government in person, Xiang rode with Prince of Xianyang Xi and Prince of Pengcheng Xie in a calf cart under strict guard.

literal: Gao was then in panic, thinking they would surely die; she also rode by the roadside weeping and escorted them to Jincheng.
idiomatic: Gao was then in panic, sure they would die; she rode by the roadside weeping and followed them to Jincheng.

literal: When Xiang was spared, Gao said: "From now on I do not wish wealth.
idiomatic: When Xiang was spared, Gao said, "From now on I want no more wealth.

literal: Only let mother and son preserve each other; with you we will sweep the market and live by labor."
idiomatic: Only let mother and son keep each other; with you we will sweep the market and live by labor."

literal: By now favor and glory were lofty and grand; they no longer spoke of the logic of ruin.
idiomatic: By then favor and glory had mounted too high for talk of ruin.

literal: Later he was slandered by Gao Zhao, who said Xiang with Hao and others plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: Later Gao Zhao slandered him, saying Xiang with Hao and others plotted rebellion.

literal: At the time Xiang was at the southern residence.
idiomatic: At the time Xiang was at the southern residence.

literal: The emperor summoned Imperial Censor Cui Liang into the forbidden precinct to investigate Xiang's greed and licentiousness, and the arbitrary acts of Hao, Liu Zhou, Chang Jixian, Chen Saojing, and the rest.
idiomatic: The emperor summoned Imperial Censor Cui Liang into the palace to investigate Xiang's greed and lust, and the arrogance of Ru Hao, Liu Zhou, Chang Jixian, Chen Saojing, and the rest.

literal: That night he was seized and confined at the southern terrace.
idiomatic: That night he was seized and confined at the southern terrace.

literal: A hundred armored guards also surrounded and guarded Xiang's residence.
idiomatic: A hundred armored guards also surrounded his residence.

literal: In the night, fearing he would panic and flee, he sent his attendant Guo Yi to open the Jincheng gate and gallop out to explain, showing the censor's impeachment.
idiomatic: Fearing panic and flight in the night, the emperor sent his attendant Guo Yi to open the Jincheng gate and gallop out with the censor's impeachment.

literal: Grand Consort Gao saw Yi and beat her head, wailing, unable to master herself.
idiomatic: Grand Consort Gao saw Yi and beat her head, wailing beyond control.

literal: Xiang said: "If it is truly as the censor impeaches, what is there to worry?
idiomatic: Xiang said, "If it is truly as the censor charges, what is there to fear?

literal: Men presented me rare and precious goods; I truly received them; if that counts as taking bribes, why should I worry?"
idiomatic: Men gave me rare treasures and I took them. If that is bribery, why should I worry?"

literal: By daylight Hao and the rest were all granted death.
idiomatic: By daylight Hao and the rest were all put to death.

literal: Prince of Gaoyang Yong and five other princes were led in to deliberate Xiang's crime.
idiomatic: Prince of Gaoyang Yong and five other princes were brought in to judge Xiang's crime.

literal: He was guarded back to the Hualin residence in a single carriage.
idiomatic: He was taken back to the Hualin residence in a single carriage under guard.

literal: Mother and wife wept together and entered where he lived; a few young male slaves and weak maidservants followed.
idiomatic: Mother and wife wept together and entered his rooms with a few young slaves and weak maids.

literal: The guard was very strict.
idiomatic: The guard was very strict.

literal: He was moved to the Ministry of the Imperial Treasury and reduced to commoner.
idiomatic: He was moved to the Ministry of the Imperial Treasury and reduced to commoner status.

literal: A separate lodge was built in the northeast corner of Luoyang county by law's confinement, limited for life, named Hall of Recalling Goodness, and Xiang was to be moved there.
idiomatic: A separate lodge was built in Luoyang's northeast corner, guarded for life, named Hall of Recalling Goodness, and Xiang was to be moved there.

literal: Then his household slaves secretly joined a faction, planning to seize him out; they secretly copied names and quietly entrusted a serving maid to pass word to Xiang.
idiomatic: Then his household slaves secretly banded to seize him out, copied names in secret, and had a serving maid pass word to Xiang.

literal: Xiang had just taken it to examine when the gate guard's chief clerk saw from afar, burst in, took it from Xiang's hand, and presented it in memorial.
idiomatic: Xiang had just taken the note to read when the gate guard's chief clerk saw from afar, burst in, snatched it from his hand, and memorialized the emperor.

literal: The emperor secretly ordered him killed.
idiomatic: The emperor secretly ordered him killed.

literal: From the time Xiang reached the treasury he had his mother and wife return to the southern residence, coming once every five days.
idiomatic: From the time he reached the treasury he sent mother and wife back to the southern residence, to visit once every five days.

literal: That night mother and wife did not come; he died at the hands of slaves and maids.
idiomatic: That night mother and wife did not come; he died at the hands of slaves and maids.

literal: An edict returned the mourning to the southern residence; all princes of the imperial clan were ordered to hurry to attend.
idiomatic: An edict sent his body back to the southern residence; every prince of the blood was ordered to attend.

literal: Funeral goods all followed the Guangling precedent.
idiomatic: Funeral goods followed the Guangling precedent in all things.

literal: When Xiang was first confined he told his mother of the affair with Gao.
idiomatic: When Xiang was first confined he told his mother of the affair with Lady Gao.

literal: His mother was greatly angry and cursed him: "You have your own wives and serving maids, young and blooming as flowers—why lie with a Goryeo slave girl and bring this crime!
idiomatic: His mother raged and cursed him: "You have wives and maids young as flowers—why lie with a Goryeo slave and bring this ruin upon us!

literal: If I get that Goryeo slave I will eat her flesh."
idiomatic: If I lay hands on that Goryeo girl I will eat her flesh."

literal: She then beat Xiang's back and both legs more than a hundred times.
idiomatic: She beat his back and both legs more than a hundred times.

literal: She wielded the staff herself until strength failed; then she had a slave take her place.
idiomatic: She wielded the staff herself until her strength failed, then had a slave take her place.

literal: Lady Gao was by nature severe; for Xiang's small faults she often added punishment, wrapping the staff in cotton.
idiomatic: Lady Gao was severe by nature; for Xiang's small faults she often punished him, wrapping the staff in cotton.

literal: By now the cotton was removed; all reached festering sores.
idiomatic: Now the cotton was stripped away; every blow brought festering sores.

literal: She also beat his consort Liu dozens of times, saying: "New wife of a great house, families matched in standing—what did you fear that you did not check your husband!"
idiomatic: She also beat his consort Liu dozens of times, crying, "New wife of a great house, families matched in standing—what did you fear that you never checked your husband!"

literal: Liu smiled and accepted the punishment; in the end she said nothing.
idiomatic: Liu smiled and took the blows; in the end she said nothing.

literal: Though Xiang's greedy and licentious faults were heard far and near, on the day of his death his crimes had no fixed name; near and far sighed in wonder.
idiomatic: Though his greed and lust were known far and wide, on the day he died his crimes had no fixed name; men near and far marveled.

literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongping an edict restored his princely rank; posthumous name Prince Ping.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongping 1 an edict restored his princely rank; posthumously he was Prince Ping.

literal: His son Hao succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Hao succeeded.

literal: Hao, styled Ziming, in youth was generous and had bold spirit.
idiomatic: Hao, styled Ziming, was generous in youth and full of bold spirit.

literal: He was Governor of Xuzhou; soon impeached by the censor and removed from the rolls.
idiomatic: He served as governor of Xuzhou, then was impeached by the censor and struck from the rolls.

literal: Later bandit chiefs Su Qinmingyuan and Chigan Qilin and others raided Bin and Hua and other prefectures; Hao's princely rank was restored and he was made Left Vice Minister and Western Route Commissioner to attack Mingyuan.
idiomatic: Later, when bandit chiefs Su Qinmingyuan and Chigan Qilin raided Bin and Hua, his princely rank was restored and he was made left vice minister and western route commissioner to attack Mingyuan.

literal: He repeatedly broke the bandits and relieved the sieges of Bin and Hua.
idiomatic: He broke the bandits again and again and lifted the sieges of Bin and Hua.

literal: Later Xiao Baoyin and others were greatly defeated at Pingliang; Hao also fled back to the capital.
idiomatic: Later Xiao Baoyin and others were routed at Pingliang; Hao also fled back to the capital.

literal: Early in Wutai he was Governor of Xiangzhou to resist Ge Rong.
idiomatic: Early in Wutai he was governor of Xiangzhou to resist Ge Rong.

literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and set up Emperor Zhuang, Hao was made Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and set up Emperor Zhuang, Hao was made grand tutor.

literal: Hao, because Ge Rong invaded south and Erzhu committed outrage, then lingered and looked about, plotting a policy for his own safety.
idiomatic: With Ge Rong pressing south and Erzhu committing outrage, Hao lingered and looked about, plotting how to save himself.

literal: When affairs did not succeed he with his son Guanshou fled to Liang.
idiomatic: When the plan failed he fled to Liang with his son Guanshou.

literal: Emperor Wu of Liang made him ruler of Wei and lent him troops and generals, ordering him north.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang made him ruler of Wei, lent him troops and generals, and ordered him north.

literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yong'an, south of Liang's capital he ascended the altar and burned the fire; era name Xiaoji year 1.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yong'an 2, south of the Liang capital, he ascended the altar and lit the sacred fire; his era was Xiaoji 1.

literal: Emperor Zhuang ordered Prince of Jiyin Huiye to resist him at Kaocheng; Huiye was captured by Hao.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang ordered Prince of Jiyin Huiye to resist him at Kaocheng; Huiye was captured.

literal: Emperor Zhuang went north in favor; Hao then entered Luoyang and changed the era to Jianwu 1.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang went north in retreat; Hao entered Luoyang and proclaimed the era Jianwu 1.

literal: Hao with several thousand men, turning in battle repeatedly victorious, held the capital and issued orders himself.
idiomatic: With a few thousand men Hao fought his way in, again and again victorious, seized the capital, and gave orders in his own name.

literal: Sentiment throughout the realm looked to his wind and government.
idiomatic: All under Heaven looked to his wind and government.

literal: He himself thought Heaven had granted it and grew quite proud and slack.
idiomatic: He thought Heaven had granted the throne and grew proud and slack.

literal: Former guests and close attendants of long standing were all favored and interfered in government affairs.
idiomatic: Old guests and close attendants were all favored and meddled in government.

literal: He also drank day and night without caring for army or state.
idiomatic: He drank day and night and cared nothing for army or state.

literal: The southern troops under his command plundered the markets; court and countryside lost hope.
idiomatic: The southern troops under his command plundered the markets; court and countryside lost hope.

literal: At the time he was also harsh in frugality; public and private were unsettled.
idiomatic: He was harsh in frugality as well; public and private life both frayed.

literal: Emperor Zhuang with Erzhu Rong returned with troops to attack Hao; Hao himself resisted at Heqiao.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang returned with Erzhu Rong to attack him; Hao met them at Heqiao.

literal: Guanshou was defeated in battle and captured.
idiomatic: Guanshou was defeated and captured.

literal: Hao himself went out by Zhuanxu to Linying and was beheaded by a soldier of Linying county.
idiomatic: Hao fled by Zhuanxu toward Linying and was beheaded by a soldier of Linying county.

literal: At first, when Hao entered Luoyang, that day there was a violent wind; he wished to enter the Changle gate; the horse was greatly startled and would not advance; men held the reins and only then entered.
idiomatic: When he first entered Luoyang that day a violent wind rose; at the Changle gate his horse panicked and would not advance until men seized the reins.

literal: There was Hengnong Yang Yanhua who told others: "Hao will surely not succeed; though he borrows imperial robes, it will not pass sixty days."
idiomatic: Yang Yanhua of Hengnong told others, "Hao will never succeed; though he borrows imperial robes, he will not pass sixty days."

literal: Remonstrating Censor Yuan Zhaoye also said: "Formerly Gengshi from Luoyang went west; at the first setting out the horses startled and ran, striking the northern palace's iron pillar; three horses all died, and Gengshi in the end did not complete the imperial position.
idiomatic: Remonstrating Censor Yuan Zhaoye also said, "When Gengshi left Luoyang for the west, his horses bolted at the start and struck the northern palace's iron pillar; three horses died, and Gengshi never finished as emperor.
